claims.claim: Model pair and scale: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B + Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 198 delta matrices; embedding and lm_head are separate (152064x3584) matrices (tie_word_embeddings=false); the full delta in fp16 is 15230566400 bytes. Source: results/fifth_pair_stage2.json.

Byte budget: uniform rank-32 on the real shapes costs 86499328 bytes (about 176x smaller than the full delta). All five Spark-generated recipes priced inside budget on real shapes; the winner down_king costs 86401024 bytes. Sources: results/fifth_pair_check1.json, results/fifth_pair_stage2.json, results/fifth_pair_build_variant.json.
Streamed randomized-SVD precompute over all 198 delta matrices: verdict PASS, 351.14 s of a 1800 s budget, peak RSS 7501.6 MB. Source: results/fifth_pair_precompute.json.

Build validation: 2144 factor files across the six configs (counted in the Flash stage2 workdir); graft check (base + full delta == instruct) max abs diff 5.82e-11; the applied factored delta matches factored.quantize_delta's product to 5.40e-11 max over sampled (matrix, rank) pairs (factor-level diffs reach 1.85e-09 from singular-vector rotation under clustered singular values; the product is the gate). Sources: results/fifth_pair_stage2.json, results/fifth_pair_product_check.json.

Stage 2 on the 24 Signet items (mean target logprob, higher is better): down_king -9.5837 (first-token accuracy 0.333), o_proj_sentinel -9.629, vocab_titans -11.2036, gate_up_monolith -13.7784, uniform_rank32 -14.4748, kv_zero_expansion -14.9005. down_king is the winner and is byte-fair. down_king's accuracy 0.333 is the highest of ALL configs on the 24, including the full delta (0.292). Source: results/fifth_pair_stage2.json.

Reference inversion (the honest complication): on the Signet 24 the full delta scores -17.7691 overall, BELOW the base model's -7.2632, so gap_closed is reported as null for every config on this pair (no recovery fraction). Mechanism, verified by a template diagnostic: under the chat template the instruct model puts probability 0.999998 on the token 'The' after 'The capital of Japan is' and only 1.93e-08 on the target continuation; rescored as raw completion (no template), the full delta beats base on knowledge (-1.325 vs -1.462) and instruction (-2.678 vs -4.127). The battery's completion-style targets measure chat-format behavior at 7B, not delta quality. Source: results/fifth_pair_template_diagnostic.json.

Held-out 96 questions: base -6.9158 (accuracy 0.073), full delta -15.9741 (accuracy 0.312), down_king -8.6939 (accuracy 0.344), uniform_rank32 -13.1583 (accuracy 0.323). down_king beats uniform by 4.464 nats at 98304 fewer bytes, and has the highest first-token accuracy of all configs; gap_closed is null again (full delta below base). Source: results/fifth_pair_heldout96.json.

Plain 1-bit baseline at 7B (BitDelta-style initialization only, no training): priced 951911192 bytes (11.0x the factored budget) and scored -11.3776 (accuracy 0.312) on the 96, worse than the 86 MB down_king patch. Source: results/fifth_pair_heldout96.json.

Memory: the streamed evals peak at about 2.2-2.35 GB RSS; the factor build peaked at 8349.5 MB; the 7B model (about 30 GB in fp32) was never held whole in memory on the 11 GB machine. Sources: eval records in results/fifth_pair_stage2.json and results/fifth_pair_heldout96.json; results/fifth_pair_build_summary.json.

Independent script recomputation of every score, bucket, subset, ranking, byte price and gap null in both results files, from the per-item rows and the architecture constants: 78 of 78 checks pass. Source: results/fifth_pair_recompute.json.

AirLLM library feasibility (lyogavin/airllm, Apache 2.0; concept credited in NOTICE.md; our runtime is our own NumPy implementation): CPU-only install was quick and clean (venv about 1.4 GB, torch 2.15.0+cpu, transformers 5.21.0); import works and CUDA is correctly reported unavailable. from_pretrained split the base model into per-layer shards and built the empty Qwen2 model, then FAILED at load after 95.1 s with 'AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled': the library's load path requires CUDA, so the real AirLLM cannot load the 7B base model on this CPU-only box without patching the library. Time-boxed and not pursued; all streaming numbers come from our own NumPy runtime, labeled AirLLM-style.

Streamed generation demo (greedy, no KV cache, both configs streamed block by block; peak RSS 4295.7 MB; 10 steps, first token after 267.18 s, per-step times [267.18, 252.71, 287.82]... s for 6 streams at once): prompt 1: base -> 'There are 366 days in a leap' | patched -> '366_Pods'; prompt 2: base -> 'To find 15% of 20' | patched -> '30'; prompt 3: base -> 'Tokyo' | patched -> 'TokyoprintStats'. Source: results/fifth_pair_stream_demo_transcript.txt.

Reports 351.14s <1800s PASS with 7501.6MB peak; no arithmetic or ordering violation.
5.82e-11 and 5.40e-11 are fp-rounding level, and product-gate with 1.85e-09 factor rotation from clustered singular values is coherent.
Full -17.7691 < base -7.2632 so gap denominator negative and null is honest; ln(1.93e-08)=-17.76 matches full mean and raw-completion reversal supports template-artifact explanation.
-8.6939-(-13.1583)=4.464 nats and 86499328-86401024=98304 bytes correct, and full -15.9741 < base -6.9158 so null gap is honest.
2.2-2.35GB and 8349.5MB peaks are <11GB, and 7.6B*4~30GB supports never-held-whole claim.
78/78 recomputation pass claim has no internal arithmetic contradiction.
CUDA assertion after sharding supports CPU-only incompatibility conclusion with clear NumPy-runtime attribution.
Transcript is reported without success overclaim, with timing/RSS and degenerate patched strings disclosed as-is.
